correctness.rationale: Marginal and two-category beta/Dirichlet–multinomial probabilities yield covariance K^2 p1 p2 (R-1). Factorization in inverse concentration t isolates increasing factors and B(t). Direct derivation gives B'/B numerator a cubic, all coefficients proved strictly positive for K>=2+choose(n-1,2) using explicit positive polynomials in n-4. The two endpoint ratios straddle 1, so continuity and strict monotonicity imply a unique crossing. Exact-rational enumeration and polynomial-identity checks were executed from the current package; they are not substitutes for the analytic proof. The claimed exact endpoint condition for R(infinity)>1 follows by an algebraic inequality. The equality boundary K=1+choose(n-1,2) is not assigned a finite-shape sign.

originality.rationale: Full-text 2017, 2020, and 2021 related literature was inspected; searched mathematical records for concentration-varying singleton–doubleton covariance aliases, negative-discount exchangeable partition equivalence and stronger coverage. The closest known results treat full DM count moments, richness-versus-frequency covariances or positive-discount infinite-type sampling. Those statements do not imply the new finite symmetric DM all-concentration one-crossing theorem. Priority remains conditional on uncovered Gibbs-partition moment literature.
residual_risks: Unindexed or non-open full-text studies might already prove monotonicity of the finite symmetric Dirichlet–multinomial singleton–doubleton ratio.
Known negative-discount Gibbs partition identities may admit an unstated corollary covering this result; database search alone cannot exclude this.

A prior published result on the same pair but different parameter line is not automatically equivalent; the claim-to-prior comparison relies on the verified finite-type versus infinite-type distinction.

value.rationale: Counts observed exactly once and twice are meaningful sparsity/diversity diagnostics (2017 microbiome literature explicitly considers both) and symmetric Dirichlet mixing is a widely used baseline for overdispersed categorical counts (2020 model literature). Proving a unique covariance sign reversal as the reinforcement parameter varies is a new structural phase classification, not merely the known raw second moment formula. The exact threshold for the normalized small-shape sign-ratio limit explains which finite alphabet sizes support the positive-dependence regime.
